Hero_Desc_Taida:
A Monatium City Hall security guard.
An elf who is great at slacking off without her superior officer noticing.
Her specialty is surfing the web behind Amelia's back. She is extremely thorough in managing her browsing history on Elfnet.
Album_Hate_Taida: Extra work just before clocking in and out.
Album_Taida1: Taida is an Elven security guard. She's neither particularly good nor bad at her job. Actually, she could do better, but shows absolutely no willingness to do so.
Album_Taida2: While Taida dislikes work and loves slacking off, she doesn't want to be unemployed. She wants to procrastinate and rest while being employed, not be carelessly idle without any backup plan.
Album_Taida3: Surprisingly, Taida performs well when given tasks. This ability developed from her past attempts to complete a full day's work in advance to slack off later. However, she has abandoned this strategy after realizing it only leads to more work assignments.
Album_Taida4: Taida connects to Elfnet regularly and whenever possible, either chatting or reading others' posts. She's well-known for her habit of ignoring business-related conversations in favor of more lighthearted ones.
Album_Taida5: Despite being a security guard, Taida is never seen actually standing guard. Her reasoning is that if someone can be stopped by her, they wouldn't get in anyway, and if they're too strong for her to stop, there's no point in trying.
Album_Taida6: When harshly scolded, she becomes overzealous about her guard duties. She starts harassing passing elves by demanding IDs and questioning the purpose of their visit, kicking out those who can't answer properly. For that reason, her slacking off can actually be more helpful.
Album_Taida7: Seeing how elementals can work just by lying down and sleeping, Taida once fell into deep contemplation. She was so absorbed in the idea that she seriously went to the library to research how to become an elemental.
LoveHero_Taida:
Can I skip training
if I follow the Master?

I'll be on standby somewhere...
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Hate1: Taida seems to have the palate of a picky child.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Hate2: She sniffed it and grimaced, furtively looked around, then quietly split when no one was looking.

Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like4: She seems to enjoy fine dining, cutting it with a fork and knife as if it were a steak.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like5: She said the taste was familiar, similar to a sour supplement she often enjoys when at work.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like6: Perhaps because it's not available in Elias, she rated this food very highly.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like7: Using the strange logic that laziness and chocolate are indispensable, she keeps eating them.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like8: She made a strange claim that mixing this with various convenience store drinks allows her to rest without stopping.
Food_ChefNote_Taida_Like9: Saying you can choose a variety of flavors with this candy, she wanted to acknowledge the sprites' confectionery skills.

LoveLetter_Taida: Hello, Master!I'm writing this to you during a brief break at work.And no, I'm definitely not avoiding my responsibilities or slacking off, okay? I appreciate how you always greet me and ask about my well-being whenever we run into each other in Monatium.But outside of work, I'd like you to see me as Taida, the one who wants to rest and enjoy some time off, not Taida the civil servant.Basically... ask someone else to take care of your busy work—ahem.See you soon.
LoveCall_Taida:
Hello, Master. This is Taida. A good idea suddenly occurred to me while I was working.

The idea is this: the Order has Apostles responsible for protecting it, correct? Just like we Monatium security officials.
How about arranging technical cooperation between them and me? I could visit the Order and teach them various Monatium security techniques.
I am absolutely, abso~lutely not suggesting this because you are generous rather than strict and working under you seems comfortable, understood?
This proposal is intended to let Monatium and the Order observe and learn from each other's methods, then develop together.

Please give my words careful consideration, Master. I look forward to a positive answer!
